content.thinking:
I'm designing a dragonbone soul scythe in a League-style Soul Reaper aesthetic, roughly 2 meters tall with a 0.9 meter blade, standing upright on a stone or obsidian plinth with a socket base so it touches the floor.

I'm considering whether to keep it a plain object or add a root joint plus a few hinge joints for a hanging soul-lantern charm or chain ornament, keeping the rig modest. For the plinth itself, I'm planning a dark, stepped hexagonal base with a glowing rune ring achieved through a separate textured disc part rather than true emissive glow.

For the scythe, I'm designing the shaft as a slight S-curved staff built from dragon-vertebrae segments along a bezier path from the plinth socket up to the blade, with the blade extending sideways in the X-Y plane so it reads fully in front view. Each vertebra segment will have a spool-like body, small transverse processes, and a dorsal spike, with a wrapped grip section near where the hand would hold it.

At the base, I'm giving it a dragon-claw spike for the butt cap digging into the plinth, and at the top the shaft terminates in a dragon skull with sweeping horns, from which a massive curved rib/wing-bone blade emerges, edged in glowing teal-green soul energy, with a floating flame orb held in the skull's jaws -- all set against a palette of bone ivory, dark purple-black metal, and gold accents against the teal soul glow.

Finalizing blade construction...

I'll generate the outer and inner curve points procedurally rather than hand-coding each one, using control points to sweep the blade's center-line from the root out to a tip positioned past the skull, keeping the point count capped at a reasonable max for a clean extrusion.

I'm thinking the blade should be built from two layered extrudes: a bone-ivory outer spine frame following the full silhouette, and a thinner glowing teal-violet soul-steel core nested inside it, working out the right relative thicknesses so the inner blade doesn't awkwardly protrude past the frame.

Working out the blade's gradient paint logic...

For the bone ribs I'm layering tube overlays on each face with mirrored thickness, plus a thin glowing edge sweep along the blade's border and glowing rune decals. For the dragon skull at the shaft's top, I'm weighing orientation options—facing forward for a front-view read versus angled up at 30° for better dimensionality from a three-quarter view.

I'm picturing the skull pitched slightly forward with an open mouth clutching a soul orb, its neck curving forward into a vertebrae collar that the blade root clamps onto with a bone claw, while a smaller curved horn-spike with a hanging soul-fire charm extends backward on the opposite side for visual balance.

Lower on the shaft, I'm adding a dragon ribcage made of five curved bone arcs that cage a glowing teal soul orb floating around the shaft, bulging outward between two collar rings for a readable, layered silhouette.

For extra flair, I'm thinking tattered cloth ribbons hanging below the blade's collar, plus a small charm cluster — beads, a mini claw, and a tassel of soul-flame cards using glowing teardrop textures. I'll also spiral tiny ghost-wisp cards up the shaft, double-sided glowing silhouettes with faint eyes, orbiting near the bone cage.

For the plinth, I'm picturing a stepped obsidian hexagonal base with a glowing rune ring carved on top, three bone talons gripping the shaft like a claw stand, and scattered bones, skulls, and soul-motes around the base.

I'm now thinking about overall proportions — footprint around 1.4m wide, scythe height roughly 2.1m, with the blade extending further on one side than the other so the weapon feels balanced rather than perfectly symmetric around x=0.

Actually simpler: a rounded hexagonal dais centered at x=0 radius 0.7, with the shaft at x=-0.2. Blade root near x=-0.2, tip around x=0.85, counter hook to -0.55, giving a bounding box roughly -0.7 to 0.85, centered close enough to zero.

Thinking through overall scale: shaft ~1.9m plus blade, total figure height ~2.2m including skull. I'm placing the dais top at y=0.16, shaft rising from there to y=1.85, skull crown spanning 1.85-2.15, and blade root at y≈1.9 curving outward to a tip near (SX+1.0, 1.35) -- mimicking the classic S-curved snath of a real scythe.

I'm giving the shaft a subtle S-curve in the Z plane and building it from vertebra-like segments: a dark central core, 22 spool-shaped vertebrae lathed along the path with slightly flared ends, and small dorsal spines pointing backward at each segment to evoke a spine-like structure.

I'm also planning transverse spikes at each vertebra but weighing the triangle budget, so I'll keep them cheap and low-poly, then mapping out the shaft zones from bottom to top -- claw-foot socket, vertebra sections with tapering radius, leather-wrapped grip, and eventually the soul cage further up.

The grip wrap continues with gold bone-clasps at its ends, then I'm layering more vertebrae and the soul cage ribs higher up, placing the cage around y1.2–1.62 with an orb at 1.4 below the blade root at 1.9. Above that I'm adding a dark gold collar where the neck vertebrae curve forward, leading into the skull positioned near the top, angled slightly downward and forward, with the blade root attaching into the neck just below it.

Now I'm working out the dragon skull itself so it doesn't collide with the blade's plane — keeping it offset forward in z so it reads as a separate element facing ahead, jaws open around a glowing soul flame. I'm sketching the cranium as an ellipsoid with a tapering snout, swept-back horns, brow and cheek spikes, glowing teal eye sockets, nostrils, and a ring of teeth along the upper jaw, sizing the whole skull around 0.28 long and 0.14 wide and orienting it along the +Z axis from a center point near (SX, 2.0, 0.1).

Positioning the lofted snout and lower jaw stations...

I need a gold/dark metal collar where the blade extrudes starting at the neck, with the blade plane sitting behind the skull so it passes through the neck naturally. I'm also adding a counter hook: a small bone horn on the opposite side curving back and up from the collar via a bezier sweep.

I'm designing a dragon claw-hook that curves down to a tapering point, with a glowing bone claw and a hanging charm chain of beads ending in a dragon-tooth with a glowing soul bead, plus a tassel or ribbon. Now I'm defining the blade's spine curve as a bezier path extending along the X axis from the collar origin.

The blade sweeps outward then curves down to a sharp point, with the back edge following the outer convex curve and the cutting edge offset inward along the concave side using a width function that ramps up toward the middle of the blade.

I'm adding sawtooth spikes along the back edge for a dragon-spine effect, with a few larger fin-like spikes, then placing curved ribs sweeping from the spine outward like dragon-wing fingers.

These look like wing membrane veins, with knuckle-like bone knobs along the spine as spheres. I'm planning the color scheme for the blade — dark violet near the spine fading to purple then teal at the edge, plus a glowing teal strip along the edge itself.

For the glow strip I'm tapering its radius along the sweep. For the paint gradient across the blade, I'm working out how to map each texel to its position relative to the spine curve, weighing brute-force sampling against a simpler closed-form approach using the outline coordinates directly since the blade lies flat in a plane.

Now I'm planning the color bands by that distance fraction: deep violet-purple near the spine with subtle swirling noise for a soul-smoke feel, transitioning to teal and bright cyan toward the edge, plus quantizing into a few cel-shaded steps for a stylized look.

For the runes, I'm thinking of placing small glowing glyph planes along the blade's centerline, oriented to tilt with the blade's curve using the tangent direction to control their roll.

Now I'm sketching three svg rune designs in teal strokes, including a runic strip symbol and a soul-flame motif.

For the palette I'm settling on bone ivory, obsidian purple-black, violet, teal glow, gold, and crimson leather tones, keeping the count under 64 flat colors with teal as the accent, and thinking through the dais as an octagonal or hexagonal form.

I'm planning a two-tiered dais with a glowing rune disk inset on top, surrounded by small bone spikes like dragon teeth and a few floating soul orbs with trails for extra atmosphere, plus carved panel inlays on the obsidian base.

Now I'm detailing the dais finish — painted obsidian with glowing crack patterns and a hexagonal lathe column for the sides — and planning claw prongs that grip the shaft's base like dragon talons. I'm also sketching joint roles for the hanging charm chain and a jaw hinge for an attached skull ornament.

I need to make sure each static part explicitly binds to the root bone rather than drifting toward the nearest chain joint, since parts attach to whichever bone or joint is closest by default. I'm planning small wrapper helper functions to keep part definitions consistent and avoid misassignment.

I'm also budgeting part counts, aiming for roughly 400-600 total by merging repeated small decorations like rivets and teeth into single parts per color, while letting the vertebrae sweeps (spools plus spikes) run to around 100 parts on their own.

I'll write a helper that merges each vertebra's cylinder and cone geometries into one combined shape, placing them in model space using matrix transforms built from position, orientation quaternions, and scale, so each vertebra becomes a single colored part rather than many loose pieces.

I realize geometries differ in indexing—spheres are indexed while icosahedrons aren't—so I'll normalize everything by converting to non-indexed geometry in the add helper, keeping position, normal, and uv attributes consistent for flat shading.

Now I'm defining the shaft's shape as a slight S-curve path using a series of points with small x/z offsets, building it through a Catmull-Rom spline for a gentle organic sway.

I'm setting up the skeleton with root and jaw joints, then sweeping the shaft core along the path with a dark iron color bound to the root bone. I'm also planning vertebrae segments spaced along the shaft, skipping the grip zone where a crimson leather wrap will spiral instead.

Working out the leather wrap stripe pattern...

Then I'm figuring out gold clasp rings at the grip ends using lathe geometry for the raised bands.

For the vertebrae, I'm approximating the spool shape using merged cylinders—wider discs at both ends with a narrower waist cylinder in between, plus a spinous process detail.

Adding spine spikes and transverse processes...

Each rib tapers with bone color and tiny end knobs, placed six around the axis. The orb glows teal at center with a bright inner core and a gold rune ring orbit, giving it that League-style magical artifact look, plus a tilted secondary ring orbit for depth. At the top I'm adding a gold-plated bone collar with eight downward-pointing fang spikes.

For the blade mount, I'm sketching a clamp styled like a dragon wing joint with a knuckle sphere and spikes where the blade root attaches, then plotting the blade's spine as a bezier curve that rises from the shaft, bends, and sweeps down to a sharp tip positioned so it clears the dais radius. I'm checking the overall bounding box to make sure the tip and the skull horns keep the total scythe height around 2.3 units.

Now I need to build the blade's outer outline by sampling points along the spine curve, computing tangents and normals to offset the edge toward the concave side, then tracing forward along the spine and back along the offset edge to form a closed, non-self-intersecting shape -- watching for cases near the tip where the curvature is tight enough that the offset width could cause the edges to cross.

I'm also considering adding a flame-like scalloped texture to the inner edge by modulating the width function with a sine wave, creating alternating serrations between the ribs.

This creates sharp tips at the rib ends with scalloped indentation between them, giving that dragon-wing blade look. I'm dialing back the scallop depth to 0.2*w so it doesn't weaken the scythe edge's silhouette, then moving to extrude the blade outline.

Writing extrude parameters...

For the spine, I'm planning a tapered bone tube following the curve of the spine points, sweeping a radius that narrows from the base toward the tip, using a bezier built from my own world-space sample points for consistency.

I'm thinking through paint budget: applying ivory grain textures selectively to the biggest surfaces (blade, dais, spine tube, maybe skull) rather than everything, estimating texel density against total painted area to keep things crisp without wasting atlas space, and considering bumping to a 4096 atlas for extra sharpness.

Now I'm working out the rib geometry for each scallop: each rib runs from a point slightly before the scallop tip on the spine out to the edge point at the tip, using a bezier curve with a bowed-out control point, and I'm deciding between a tapered round cross-section or a flat box section with small z-offsets on both faces for thickness.

I'm adding spiky bone knuckles at the rib start, small claw spikes protruding past the edge tips, and a row of six decreasing-size cone spikes along the spine at specific intervals for a bony ridge effect, plus planning rune glyph decals placed in the mid-blade areas between ribs.

Then I'm placing four glyph planes at specific blade positions below the spine, oriented along the tangent and mirrored on both faces with a glow effect, and building a glowing sweep along the entire cutting edge path (including scallop points) using a dense polyline of sampled points so the sweep tessellation follows the curvature smoothly with rounded corners at the scallop tips.

Now I'm designing the ghost soul-sprites: teardrop-shaped bodies with dark cutout eyes and wispy tails, placed on transparent cards and spiral-positioned around the shaft between two height levels with radially increasing radius so they drift upward and outward, using a flow function that maps each card index to a precomputed direction. Next I'm planning teal flame card details for the skull's brow and dais corner teeth.

I'm also figuring out the dais's bone-fang posts with attached flame cards, merged glowing soul-mote octahedra floating around the structure, and a hanging charm off the hook tip -- a chain of linked beads ending in a dragon-claw with a teal gem and ribbons, where the hook itself follows a curved bone sweep path from the collar down to a tip, with charm segments positioned progressively below the attachment point.

Now I'm working out the charm chain mechanics: creating a named bone chain for the joints, sweeping a thin cord along it with gold beads, and attaching a dragon-tooth spike and glowing soul gem at the tip joint. I'm also planning crimson tattered ribbons hanging from the charm as flat extruded slabs rather than true cloth simulation, keeping them static and attached to the charm bones.

Then I shift to defining the skull geometry in a local coordinate frame, mirroring left/right across the center point, with a scaled sphere for the cranium, wedge-shaped brow ridges, and a lofted snout built from stacked profile stations extending forward from the skull's origin.

For the mouth, I'm placing nostril bumps near the snout tip, rows of downward-pointing teeth spikes along the jawline with larger fangs at the front, and a lower jaw lofted from a hinge joint down to an open tip to give it a slightly agape, menacing expression.

I'm adding upward teeth spikes on the lower jaw and a glowing teal flame orb inside the mouth to suggest an inner fire, then building the eyes as dark flattened sockets with small glowing teal spheres nested inside, tilted slightly for a slanted, menacing look. Now I'm working out the horn geometry, sweeping curved shapes from the cranium base outward and back using control points to give them a swept, dramatic silhouette.

I'm adding ivory-to-darker-tip gradient coloring to the horns, smaller cheek spikes pointing back-out, jaw frill spikes, and a spiky spine crest along the back of the skull between the horns. I'm also placing a small glowing octahedron gem on the forehead as a runic accent, and confirming the skull orientation faces forward relative to the dais, then shifting focus to building the dais's first tier as a hexagonal lathed shape with a chamfered edge.

Now I'm working out the tiered dais geometry -- sizing tier1 and tier2 heights and radii, placing a textured inlay disc on top of tier2, and figuring out its facing direction and orientation. I'm wrestling with how to center the dais relative to the off-center shaft, since centering purely on the shaft versus centering the overall bounding box gives different results, and I'm testing a shifted center value to get a more balanced bounding box for the whole weapon.

I'm now designing the bone claw prongs gripping the shaft -- curved bezier shapes from the dais top up to a grip point, tapered to points, with small knuckle balls and a gold clamp ring. Then I'm planning the gold trim details on the dais tiers, debating whether to build them as swept hexagonal outlines or as an extruded hexagon shape, while being unsure of the exact vertex orientation the lathe segments produce.

Working out the extrude orientation so the hexagon outline sits flat with thickness extending upward, I'm sizing two tiers (wider base, narrower top) and planning a third thin top ring, plus gold trim frames swept along the tier edges, bone dragon-fang spikes at the hex corners, and small glowing teal gem accents along the tier sides.

For the dais surface, I'm writing a paint function that uses cell noise to generate crack patterns in teal against a mottled dark obsidian base, applied across all faces. I'm also adding scattered glowing crystal shards near the dais corners, and finalizing the ivory, bone, and obsidian color palette.

Now I'm rounding out the full palette with violet, teal, gold, and crimson tones, around twenty colors total, and starting to check which math and path APIs are available for the actual construction code.

I set up root joint placement and direction, then start writing helper functions for merging geometry by color and attaching glow materials to grouped parts.

Writing helper functions...

Still defining geometry helpers...

I'm sketching a vertebra builder that orients each segment along a local frame, aligning it with a tangent direction and offsetting the neural spine backward and upward relative to the spine's roughly vertical path.

Now I'm placing vertebrae by walking along the shaft curve, sampling points and tangents at each position, then adding cage ribs spaced at 60-degree azimuth intervals around the shaft.

I'll keep the shaft perfectly straight and vertical for a clean look, simplifying it to a basic polyline between the top and bottom points without needing extra curve calculations.

Now I'm designing the cage ribs that curve outward from the shaft, using bezier paths with varying radius for a slight bulge, with gold spherical joints at each end and ivory coloring for a bone-like material. I'm considering adding small spikes at the rib midpoints and thinking through how six ribs would distribute around the shaft when viewed from the front.

For the central orb, I'm layering a glowing teal outer shell with a brighter teal core inside, then considering a faceted "soul gem" look with an icosahedron or octahedral shape plus thin glowing halo rings sweeping around it for extra visual interest.

Settling on the final orb: a low-poly flat icosahedron core with two tilted gold orbit rings catching the light, plus small teal motes circling it. For the ghost wisps and flames I'll render those as SVG elements, and I'm planning the grip wrap paint details, gold clasps near the handle, and now sketching out the neck vertebrae leading up to the skull, starting with a gold collar ring and three curving vertebra segments.

Working out exact placement: the shaft ends where the neck meets the base of the cranium sphere, with a gold lathed collar below it and a wrist knuckle joint higher up. I'm placing small tilted vertebrae beneath the cranium center and now positioning the blade root origin and a mounting knuckle sphere where the blade connects to the neck structure.

Now I'm designing paired bone clamp plates flanking the blade root, tapered triangular shapes extruded with slight thickness and bevels, dotted with gold rivets on each side.

Still writing spine curve...

I want the scallop tips to form sharp cusps at the knots while the curve between them dips concavely, giving an asymmetric dragon-wing feel rather than plain symmetric arcs, so I'll skew the interpolation with a power curve to bias the swing toward one side.

I'm sampling the edge offset at both uniform points and exact knot locations, then checking for self-intersection by comparing the offset width against the local curvature radius of the spine -- the offsets are safely smaller than the radius everywhere along the curve, so the polygon should stay simple.

Near the root though, the closing edge from the offset point back to the spine start cuts diagonally rather than vertically, which looks a bit off before the root plate covers it; I'm considering reshaping that root boundary to be more vertical instead.

Simplifying by adjusting the spine's starting tangent to be flatter at the base so the initial rise is gentler, then letting the curve arch up more dynamically through the middle control points before tapering at the tip.

The tip curls downward steeply, consistent with a scythe-like silhouette, and I want to wrap it in a tapering bone tube that narrows toward a sharp point. For rendering, I'm precomputing sample points along the spine and lower-edge normal curves, then writing a paint function that finds the nearest spine sample for any pixel to determine blade thickness and shading.

I'm defining color bands based on the signed distance across the blade width, blending in noise so the violet-to-teal gradient reads as soul-smoke rather than flat stripes.

I'm leaning toward a painterly smooth gradient with a few darker streak lines at specific contour values rather than a hard cel-shaded look, implemented through a color ramp function over stops. I still need to work out the rib placement running from the blade's base point to the knot on both faces.

For the control curve I'm computing a midpoint lerp between start and end offset by a small bow along the tangent, plus a short spike extension at the tip for a claw-like point. I'm now sketching out the counter-hook shape on the opposite side with a sequence of path points, positioning its tip so a charm can attach partway along its length.

I'm hanging a charm from a point near the hook's tip, building it as a short chain of segments down to a dragon-tooth pendant, adding gold bead details along the joints and a decorative clamp ring where the hook meets the base, plus small merged-cone spikes along the hook's top edge.

Now I'm placing a glowing soul-gem shape just above the tooth and adding crimson ribbon tassels tied to that joint, along with flame-topped corner posts for the dais.

For textures, I'm generating a rune-disc SVG with concentric teal rings and a repeating series of rotated rune glyph strokes spaced evenly around the circle. Writing SVG code...

I'm also sketching smaller rune glyph textures for the blade, using compact path designs scaled so the stroke widths stay crisp at low resolution.

Now I'm drafting a ghost texture with a teardrop-shaped body path and a pale teal fill color.

I'll add an inner glow with eye ellipses and a small mouth, rooting the ghost's tail at the bottom of its frame so it appears to float upward. Then I'm planning a flame glyph with layered teal, lighter, and white core paths, while deciding to skip extra trim and emblem details for now.

Skipping decorative runes and filigree, I'll use a mottled ivory paint material for the skull parts and keep painted components sharing one material. I'll also add glowing teal glyph decals on the blade faces and consider thin glowing ring bands on the horns using merged torus geometry oriented along the shaft.

Working out horn band placement next, computing torus orientation and radii that taper along each horn, then setting up joint hierarchy with explicit bone parameters for the skull and jaw so everything attaches properly to the root.

For merging geometry, I'll key the merge bag by both color and bone name together, so parts sharing a color but belonging to different bones (like skull versus jaw) stay separate. I need to check the builder exports to confirm the Joint type is available for import.
